raw_evidence.policy: Raw evidence is never published. The author keeps it privately on one laptop disk (a single copy, by accepted risk) indefinitely, and it is available on request, verifiable against this SHA256 inventory. If that disk is lost, these hashes point at evidence that no longer exists.

reads_as: CPU, memory, gaps, bandwidth and cost are diagnostics and add no gate. ENet loss is a smoothed estimate, not a measured fraction of datagrams dropped.

cleanup.statement: Every owned resource was verified absent through authenticated provider reads.

claim.statement: Confirmed 30 players on this rented pair: three valid five-minute passes. An observed candidate, not provider-wide capacity.

peers.loss_estimate_peer_peak_scope: the highest single smoothed reading of any one bot in the window, a diagnostic that decides nothing: the gate reads the per-second mean over bots
peers.loss_estimator: ENet smoothed estimate of reliable commands lost

trajectory.scope: One entry per held second. These are diagnostics and decide nothing. The Tick series count from the start of the narrowest interval on the server's clock and the ENet series from the window start on the bot's clock, so one index can differ between them by the clock mapping. An entry with no reading is null.

separate_from_cax11: DigitalOcean evidence only. It is not a CAX11 result, satisfies no part of the historical CAX11 gate and shows nothing about ARM versus x86.
synthetic_fixture: Synthetic. Nothing ran: every number is arithmetic from fixture recorder files, on a scripted clock, against a fake provider and fake guests. It shows what the controller and exporter do with those bytes and nothing about any host, capacity or cost.
